config.pageTitle: AQA GCSE Religious Studies A: Islam Revision
config.footerNote: Original practice questions written to the AQA GCSE Religious Studies A (8062) specification. Not past-paper material. Model answers are indicative exemplars, not official AQA mark schemes; other well-argued answers can gain full credit.

Beliefs.1: 1-mark multiple choice (AO1): one mark for the single correct letter.
Beliefs.2: 2-mark 'Give two…' / 'Name two…' (AO1): one mark for each correct, distinct point. No development required.
Beliefs.4: 4-mark 'Explain two ways / two contrasting…' (AO1): for each of two points, 1 mark for a simple explanation and 2 marks for a detailed explanation (point + development). Where the question asks for contrasting beliefs or influence, the two points must genuinely differ or be applied to Muslim life.
Beliefs.5: 5-mark 'Explain two… Refer to sacred writings or another source of Muslim belief and teaching' (AO1): for each of two points, 1 mark for a simple and 2 marks for a detailed explanation; plus 1 mark for a relevant, accurate reference to sacred writing (Qur'an, Hadith) or another source of Muslim belief and teaching.
Beliefs.12: 12-mark evaluation (AO2). Answers are marked on levels. Level 4 (10-12): a well-argued response that gives reasoned consideration to different points of view, with logical chains of reasoning leading to a judgement supported by accurate knowledge of Muslim teaching. Level 3 (7-9): reasoned consideration of different points of view with logical chains of reasoning drawing on relevant knowledge. Level 2 (4-6): reasoned consideration of one point of view, or recognition of different points of view each supported by reasons. Level 1 (1-3): a point of view with a reason stated in support. Up to 3 further marks for spelling, punctuation and grammar are available on 12-mark answers in the Beliefs section. (Paraphrased summary of AQA's published approach - not an official mark scheme.)
